section_summary.extract_value: This section describes Study 2, an experiment manipulating appearance versus health exercise frames and guilt versus no-guilt (via a magazine-article style manipulation) to test whether guilt (introjected regulation) mediates the effect of appearance-based exercise motives on body anxiety. It references an initial cross-sectional study and hypothesizes that the guilt manipulation will increase post-test guilt and, in turn, predict body anxiety primarily among participants in the guilt condition.
section_summary.evidence_source: "In our second study, to test the causal links between these variables, appearance vs. health frames for exercise were manipulated at the same time as inducing guilt vs. no guilt regarding exercise behavior, using a magazine article style of manipulation, as successfully used in previous research (Aubrey, 2010)."; "The initial cross-sectional study suggests that introjected regulation shares considerable variance with both appearance goals for exercise and body image."
